biography.plain_text: Joseph Vittoria was an American business executive who led Avis as chairman and chief executive. Educated in civil engineering at Yale and business at Columbia, he worked in car rental before moving into other ventures. He later chaired Puradyn Filter Technologies, where he was also a substantial shareholder and lender.

long_biography.plain_text:
American executive Joseph Vittoria helped employees become owners of Avis through a leveraged buyout. Addressing an employee-ownership conference, he pointed to faster growth and debt repayment ahead of schedule as early results. The company had also begun allocating shares to workers, giving them a direct interest in the business.

At Travel Services International, the company he founded after leaving car rental, Vittoria assembled cruise retailers, airline consolidators and hotel-booking services. He introduced a common trading name, The Travel Company, to present the acquired businesses to customers under one identity. Acquisitions also brought specialist capabilities, including an alumni-tour operator whose direct-marketing experience he wanted other divisions to use.
